The circumstances, and the habits of life, which these circumstances occasion, have doubtless a great influence upon the character, the extent, and the bounds of our faculties; but nature herself often modifies them in a way so peculiar, that it would be absurd to ascribe them to any other origin. If ever there was a capacity of intellect, formed for receiving and improving every idea embraced by the circle of human knowledge, it was that of Diderot; his head was naturally the most encyclopédique of any that ever existed.
